full_judgment: 11. Therefore, the argument that the scope of section 491 CrPC is limited and narrower than that of Article 102 of the Constitution has no force. Its scope is not hedged by constitutional limitation for the reasons that in the Constitutional provision it is to be seen whether the detenu is being held with any lawful authority and in a matter under section 491 CrPC it is only required to be seen whether the detention order is illegal and or improper. Here in the present case, the order of detention having been made in colourable exercise of the power it cannot be said that the provision of section 491 CrPC is not applicable. The objects is to safeguard the liberty of the people by way of exercising the right in the nature of habeas corpus to ensure the protection of the citizen and, therefore, we are of the view that section 491 authorises the High Court Division to enquire whether the detenu is illegally and improperly detained in public or private custody.
